study.title: Evidence of timing effects on acupuncture: A functional magnetic resonance imaging study
study.study_design: Within-subject crossover fMRI study comparing acupuncture at two time periods in healthy volunteers and post-stroke patients
study.randomization: The sequence of the two sessions was randomized across the subjects
study.disease_condition: subcortical ischemic stroke (patient group); healthy volunteers (control group)
study.inclusion_criteria: Patient group: subcortical ischemic stroke, first-ever stroke >6 months prior to enrollment, right-handed, no acupuncture therapy experience, no history of psychiatric or neurological disorders. Control group: right-handed, no acupuncture therapy experience, no history of psychiatric or neurological disorders.
study.exclusion_criteria: Head motion of >2.5 mm of translation or >2.5° of rotation in any direction

conditions.scan_context: fMRI acquired during manual acupuncture stimulation at ST36 in morning session
fMRI acquired during manual acupuncture stimulation at ST36 in afternoon session
Rest blocks alternating with acupuncture blocks in block design; used as control condition in contrasts

interventions.procedure_label_exact: Manual acupuncture at ST36 between 7:00 a.m. and 9:00 a.m.
interventions.anatomical_location_exact: tibialis anterior muscle, four fingerbreadths below the lower margin of the patella and one fingerbreadth across from the anterior crest of the tibia
interventions.needle_size_exact: 0.3 mm in diameter and 40 mm in length
interventions.manipulation_exact: needle inserted at a depth of 1.0-2.0 cm with a frequency of 2 Hz
interventions.deqi_intended_exact: 'De qi', a composite of unique sensations, was to be achieved through needle manipulation
interventions.needle_retention_exact: 30 sec per acupuncture block, 6 acupuncture blocks
interventions.session_duration_exact: 360 sec total (12 blocks of 30 sec each)
interventions.treatment_period_exact: two sessions applied with an interval of seven days
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: instructed to lie quietly and to keep their eyes closed; foam cushions used to minimize head movement; earplugs used to reduce noise interference
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: qi is strongest on the stomach meridian of Foot-Yangming between 7:00 a.m. and 9:00 a.m., which indicates that the optimum time for acupuncture at the Foot-Yangming is between 7:00 a.m. and 9:00 a.m.

extraction_notes.note: No quantitative deqi/sensation scores are reported. The paper states de qi was assessed by interview following each scan but provides no numeric values, group comparisons, or statistical tests for this measure.
No expectancy, credibility, or blinding success measures were reported or assessed in this study.
No adverse events section is present in the paper. It is unclear whether adverse events occurred or were monitored.

Coordinates for the main activation contrasts (acupuncture > rest for each arm and condition separately) are not tabulated. Only Figure 2 shows these activations but coordinates cannot be reliably read from the figure description provided.

The abstract states 'significant regions in the healthy subjects included the prefrontal cortex, cingulum, thalamus and cerebellum' for the timing effect. Table II labels the frontal regions as 'Middle frontal gyrus' and 'Superior frontal gyrus' rather than 'prefrontal cortex'. These are consistent but not identical descriptions.

The paper refers to the 'left cingulum' in the abstract and Discussion section but Table II labels the cluster as 'Posterior cingulum' at coordinates -12, -39, 18. Both descriptions are preserved in the extraction.

The flip angle for the functional sequence is listed as 90° and the FOV as 240x240 mm, but slice thickness, number of slices, matrix size, and in-plane resolution are not reported, making full replication of the acquisition parameters impossible.

The paper states the threshold for the timing effect contrasts (Table II) as 'P<0.001 (uncorrected) at the voxel level, P<0.05 (familywise error corrected) at the cluster level' in the Table II footnote. The methods section states 'P<0.001 (uncorrected) at the voxel level, with a cluster size of 20 voxels' for the main activation contrasts. These are two distinct thresholding procedures applied to different analyses.
The paper does not report group-level coordinates for the main activation contrasts (acupuncture-rest within each condition); results are only described narratively in the text and shown in Figure 2.
No between-group (healthy vs stroke) direct comparison contrast is reported. The paper describes differences qualitatively in the Discussion.

The 'R' hemisphere label for the Superior frontal gyrus cluster at coordinates (6, 39, 45) in Table II is ambiguous given the near-midline x-coordinate. The table labels it 'R' and this is preserved exactly.
The 'L' hemisphere label for the Cuneus cluster at coordinates (3, -84, 39) in Table II is ambiguous given the near-midline x-coordinate. The table labels it 'L' and this is preserved exactly.

The paper does not report TR/TE/FOV for structural MRI sequence in the same detail as for the functional sequence (flip angle, number of slices, voxel size not reported for structural sequence either).
No information is provided on whether high-pass or low-pass temporal filtering was applied during preprocessing.
No information is provided on global signal regression.
The paper does not specify how many (if any) subjects were excluded due to excessive head motion.
